functions.name: Effect4.Program.NativeAtom.typeOf
functions.note: DI-78: the isSome and getOrElse argument patterns accept a syntactic option; every listed non-option type refuses. Both sites and their complete refusal sets are intentional.

functions.name: Effect4.Program.NativeAtom.projectProduct
functions.note: Both projections delegate to this one classifier. Products, unions and never have explicit arms; every listed alternative refuses. Its value-membership theorem is NativeAtom.projectProduct_typed.

functions.name: Effect4.Program.Ty.renderRaw
functions.note: DECISION, not a fix (seat-audit.md R-A1): `| .nat | .int => "number"` (src/Effect4/Program/Eff.lean:74) compiles to a default arm, so an appended Ty constructor would silently render "number". The cover pins the two the tree meant; a third is a refusal.

functions.name: Effect4.Program.Val.hasTy
functions.note: DECISION, not a fix (seat-audit.md R-A2, register DI-09/DI-17): site 0 is `| _ => false` (src/Effect4/Program/Typed.lean:73), so `never`, `int`, `except` and `causeOf` are silently uninhabited and an appended constructor would join them; site 1 is the inner match on `.list` at :71. The cover pins today's four; a fifth is a refusal.

functions.name: Effect4.Schema.Codec.isSupported
functions.note: DI-95 (fixed 2026-09-18): the classifier lists its positive arms (never, unit, nat, string, bool, lit, and the containers) and closes with `| _ => false`, so this default absorbs the NEGATIVE class — handle, int, fiberOf, refOf, deferredOf, var, unknown — exactly the types encodeRaw/decodeRaw refuse. An appended constructor lands here, unsupported, until it is given an arm in all three.

functions.name: Effect4.Program.Authoring.ServiceDef.receiver
functions.note: A method's receiver is the first factor of its product request; a request that is not a product is the receiver itself.

functions.name: Effect4.Program.loopResultAt
functions.note: Only `iterate` has a result term; every other form finishes a loop with unit.

functions.name: Effect4.Program.Denote.Straight
functions.note: The existing classifier now lives in Program/Fragment and is reachable from the runtime API. These constructors remain outside the fragment; moving the owner does not widen admission.

functions.name: Effect4.Run.rowOf
functions.note: Only an external operation names a host row of the run's table; every built-in operation names none.

functions.name: Effect4.Program.Denote.Straight
functions.note: Straight admits only built-in synchronous operations; asynchronous and program rows are refused.

note: Effect4's case-site policy for `Conform.Lcnf.Cases`. SEEDED from a measured scan at seat/audit (`--seed-policy`), then annotated by hand on the two rows that are decisions rather than facts (`Ty.renderRaw`, `Val.hasTy`). It is a PIN, not a proof: it records what the compiled code does today so that tomorrow's drift is a red row. Regenerate the seed with `--seed-policy` and diff; never overwrite the notes. REMOVED 2026-09-10 (idiomatic pass, audit seat): the rule for `Effect4.Program.compileEff` on `Effect4.Program.NativeOp`. That case site was never in the source — the compiler created it by specialising `NativeOp.row` at `.external` — and at `ae85bd6` the compiled code no longer has it, with NO change under src/ between the two commits (`git diff dba71eb..ae85bd6 -- src/` is empty). A case-site count is a count of compiler output read out of a BUILD DIRECTORY, so a gate must build `Effect4` before it scans. If the compiler creates the site again, `unlisted: refuse` catches it as one named row, which is the behaviour this policy wants.
